translation_rules: Prefer stdin read + token parsing; avoid Scanner-style logic.
Use read_to_string + split_whitespace by default (handles multi-line).
If input is large, use byte-based scanner (read_to_end + next_i64).
Parse ints as i64; cast to i32/usize only at the use-site.
Accumulate output in String and print once.

translation_rule_map.usize index: Rust arrays/Vec require usize indices; Java uses int freely.
translation_rule_map.n+1 sizing: 1-indexed arrays in Java need Vec of length n+1 in Rust.
translation_rule_map.bounds/offsets: i-1 / i+1 patterns must be guarded and casted safely.

translation_rules: If a variable is used inside indexing (a[i], a[i+k]), make it usize in Rust (or cast at index site).
Cast computed indices at the last moment: a[(i+k) as usize], not everywhere.
If Java uses 1..=n indexing, allocate vec![..; n+1] and keep index range 1..=n.
When Java uses i-1 or i+1 in indices, ensure the loop bounds prevent underflow/overflow before casting to usize.
For k-1 indices, ensure k>=1 before indexing to avoid usize underflow.
Prefer Vec<T> over fixed arrays for n read from input; use vec![init; n].
For 2D arrays: use vec![vec![init; m]; n] (clear) or a flat Vec<T> with idx=r*m+c (faster).

translation_rule_map.i64 default: Use i64 for CP math; cast to usize only for indexing.
translation_rule_map.i128 mul: Safe (a*b)%MOD: compute in i128 then cast.
translation_rule_map.norm mod: Keep results in [0,MOD): add MOD before %.
translation_rule_map.bitmask typed: Use u64/usize masks; type shifts (1u64<<(k as u32)).

translation_rules: Default numeric type i64; counters usize.
mod mul: ((a as i128*b as i128)%(MOD as i128)) as i64.
mod sub/neg: (x%MOD+MOD)%MOD or (a-b+MOD)%MOD.
Apply %MOD after each add/mul in loops.
inv (prime MOD): mod_pow(a, MOD-2).
Bitmask: mask u64; bit=1u64<<(i as u32); test (mask&bit)!=0.

examples.rust_translation: x=(x+(((a as i128*b as i128)%(MOD as i128)) as i64))%MOD;

translation_rule_map.PriorityQueue→BinaryHeap: Rust heap is max-heap; use Reverse for min-heap.
translation_rule_map.Queue/Deque→VecDeque: BFS/2-pointer windows with push/pop both ends.
translation_rule_map.Sorting: Arrays.sort→arr.sort(); use reverse or custom cmp for descending.
translation_rule_map.argmax: If map used only for max label, track (best_sum,best_label) instead.

translation_rules: ArrayList<T>→Vec<T>; use Vec::with_capacity(n) when size known.
HashMap counting: *map.entry(k).or_insert(0) += 1;
HashMap getOrDefault: map.get(&k).unwrap_or(&0).
HashSet: set.contains(&x); set.insert(x);
Min-heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<T>>; push Reverse(val), pop unwrap.0.
Queue: VecDeque; push_back/pop_front for BFS.
Sorting: vec.sort() ascending; vec.sort_by(|a,b| b.cmp(a)) descending.
If Java builds Map<sum,label> just to print max label, skip map; track best (sum,label) directly.

translation_rule_map.bytes: Rust String not indexable; use s.as_bytes()[i].
translation_rule_map.split filter: Java split may yield empty; filter empties in Rust.
translation_rule_map.digit→idx: Digit char to index: (c-b'0') as usize.

translation_rules: Reassignments need let mut.
Pass large Vec/String as & or &mut.
Avoid moves; iterate by borrow: for &x in v.iter().
For in-place updates prefer indexing (a[i]=...), not moving elements.
clone() only if borrowing can't work.
String/char ops: let b=s.as_bytes(); b[i]==b'X'/b'.'/b'0'.
split("X"): s.split("X").filter(|t|!t.is_empty()).
Digit to index: (c-b'0') as usize.
If borrow conflict: compute val first, then assign.
